subject: Retail LLM fit assessment + procurement path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Wu <samantha.wu@acmeretail.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Retail LLM fit assessment + procurement path

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our conversation and suggested next steps so we can align with your procurement timeline.

Pain points you described
- Search relevance for product QA and chat has regressed during holiday peaks; current embeddings pipeline struggles with SKU-heavy descriptions.
- Sporadic timeouts during peak traffic; 95th/99th tail latency often spikes and causes degraded UX.
- Cost unpredictability from current vendor (egress + per-request multipliers) and lack of control over quantization/latency tradeoffs.

Current stack you shared
- On-prem vector store (Redis) for nearest-neighbors
- Vendor-managed model endpoints for generation and embeddings (no pinned model versions)
- Internal data residency requirement for customer PII and purchase history

Success criteria we heard
- 99th percentile response time < 300ms for short chat prompts under production load
- Improved top-5 retrieval precision for QA flows (benchmarks to share)
- Predictable unit economics: target cost ceiling for 1M interactions / month
- SOC2 + ability to host in VPC (required for next phase)

What we recommend next
1) Pilot (8-week) scope: integration with your Redis store, run embeddings locally or in your VPC, validate latency and retrieval precision with a small product subset.
2) Stakeholders & procurement: identify decision owner(s) — engineering lead + procurement + security.
3) Commercial guardrails for pilot: pilot discount, capped committed units, and clear SLOs for response time.

Attachments: PoC-scope-v1.pdf (poC tasks and success criteria), redwood-pricing-band.xlsx (initial commercial bands).

Ask: Can you confirm the decision owner and preferred procurement cadence? If helpful, we can share a short SOW draft and a template MSA (to start parallel legal review).

Availability: I can host a 30-min procurement sync later this week. Suggested slots: Thu 7/22 10–11am PT or Fri 7/23 9–10am PT.

Looping in Karthik (solutions) to confirm the technical checklist and Ben (account lead) to align commercial guardrails.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Samantha / Tom / Lisa —

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation. Looping in Ben to confirm commercial guardrails and Karthik for technical runbook items.

Quick answers / next actions:
- Security contact: please send SOC2 request to security@redwood.com and I’ll ensure our security team responds within 48 hours. Karthik, can you prepare the KV/embedding integration checklist for their VPC setup?
- Pilot SOW: I attached a draft (draft-sow-acme.docx) with an 8-week scope: week 0 onboarding & infra prep, weeks 1–4 integration + telemetry, weeks 5–7 load testing & tuning, week 8 evaluation & handoff.
- Pricing: for the pilot we typically offer a capped committed unit with a 20% pilot discount; Ben will confirm the exact band and provide a short Milestone-based payment schedule.

Commercial guardrails we propose for the procurement packet:
- Pilot cap: commit up to 250k inference units for the pilot period
- Price band: X–Y per 1k tokens (Ben to confirm specific values)
- SLA targets: 99th < 300ms for target flows during test harness runs

Suggested next meeting: Thu 7/22 10:00–10:30 PT (procurement + security + Ben + Karthik). If that works, Ben and I will prepare the one-pager (SOW + commercial bands) and share before the call.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.
